title: Monster Face Pie
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A golden vegetable-and-beef pie decorated with an expressive, kid-friendly monster face for a Halloween dinner table.
ingredients: sliced olives, cheese and peppers for the face
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper so the finished pie can be moved without disturbing its decorated top.
Warm the olive oil in a skillet, then cook the onion and carrot with a pinch of salt until the vegetables soften and smell sweet rather than raw.
Add the beef and break it into small pieces, cooking until no pink remains before stirring in tomato paste, thyme and black pepper.
Pour in the stock and simmer until the filling is moist but thick enough to mound on a spoon; cool it for ten minutes before it meets the pastry.
Place one pastry sheet on the tray, spoon the cooled filling into the centre, and leave a clean border so the two pastry layers can seal properly.
Brush the border with beaten egg, place the second sheet over the filling, and crimp the edges firmly with a fork to keep steam and juices inside.
Use olives, cheese and pepper pieces to make a cheerful monster face, then cut a few small vents away from the decorations so the pastry can release steam.
Brush the exposed pastry with egg and bake until deeply golden and crisp, then rest the pie for ten minutes before cutting clean slices.
tips: Cool the filling briefly so the bottom pastry stays crisp.
commonMistakes: A wet filling can split the pastry and make the base soggy.
substitutions: Use cooked lentils in place of half the beef for a lighter filling.
storage: Refrigerate covered leftovers for up to three days and reheat in the oven.

title: Finger-Shaped Cheese Sticks
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Crisp cheese pastry sticks with almond nails and a herby finish, made for a playful Halloween snack board.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and line a large tray with baking paper, leaving room between each stick so the pastry can puff evenly.
Unroll the pastry on a lightly floured surface and scatter mozzarella, Parmesan and Italian seasoning over one half without piling cheese at the edges.
Fold the bare half over the cheese, press gently to seal, and roll once with a pin so the filling is held in a thin, even layer.
Cut the pastry into narrow strips, then lightly pinch one end of each strip to create a rounded fingertip shape rather than a blunt rectangle.
Brush every strip with beaten egg and press one almond at the rounded end, leaving the rest of the pastry visible as the edible finger nail.
Score a few shallow lines across each strip with the back of a knife; do not cut through the pastry, because the stick needs to stay intact.
Bake until the sticks are puffed, browned and the cheese has melted into the layers, rotating the tray once if one side colours faster.
Cool for five minutes so the cheese settles, then serve warm with marinara in a separate bowl for dipping.
tips: Keep the pastry cold until it goes into the oven for the best layers.
commonMistakes: Overfilling the strips lets cheese leak and burn on the tray.
substitutions: Use a small slice of red pepper in place of an almond for a nut-free nail.
storage: Store refrigerated for two days and re-crisp in a hot oven.

title: Zombie Meatloaf
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A tender glazed meatloaf with olive eyes and pepper hair, designed as a cheerful Halloween centrepiece rather than a scary dish.
ingredients: olives and green bell pepper strips
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a loaf pan or small roasting dish so the cooked meatloaf can be lifted out without breaking its shape.
Combine the beef, onion, breadcrumbs, egg, milk, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce and garlic powder in a bowl, mixing only until no dry crumbs remain.
Press the mixture into a compact loaf with a gently rounded top; packing it too firmly makes the finished slices dense instead of tender.
Bake the loaf uncovered until it is nearly cooked through, then brush the surface with barbecue sauce to create a glossy, savoury glaze.
Return it to the oven until the centre reaches a safe cooked temperature, then let it rest so its juices redistribute before decorating.
Set olive halves into small cheese circles for eyes and tuck thin green-pepper strips across the top as playful zombie hair.
Arrange the decorations while the loaf is warm but not steaming hot so they stay visible instead of sliding into the glaze.
Slice with a sharp knife and serve with roasted vegetables, keeping the decorated end intact for a fun first presentation.
tips: Use a thermometer instead of relying only on colour in the centre.
commonMistakes: Skipping the rest makes the loaf shed juices when sliced.
substitutions: Ground turkey can replace beef, with an extra tablespoon of milk for tenderness.
storage: Refrigerate slices for up to three days and reheat until hot.

title: Monster Hand Ham and Cheese Board
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: An easy Halloween grazing board that turns ham, cheese, crackers and fresh produce into a friendly monster-hand display.
instructions: Choose a large clean board and place a small bowl of olives or mustard near one corner so the board has an anchor before the hand shape is built.
Fold the ham slices into loose ribbons and arrange them in a palm shape, keeping the centre generous enough to hold cheese cubes.
Build five fingers from alternating ham folds and cheese cubes, making the thumb shorter and set at a natural angle to the rest of the hand.
Press a blanched almond at each fingertip as a playful nail, using a tiny dab of mustard only if a piece will not stay in place.
Fill the centre of the palm with cheese cubes, then frame it with cucumber, carrots and grapes so the hand silhouette remains clear from above.
Fan crackers around the open areas rather than covering the hand, and tuck a few olives into gaps for contrast and easy snacking.
Check that every ingredient can be reached without moving the hand shape, then add serving tongs or small forks for a clean shared board.
Keep chilled until serving time and refresh any cut vegetables with a paper towel if moisture begins to collect on the board.
tips: Build the hand first, then fill the empty areas around it.
commonMistakes: Adding crackers underneath the ham makes the hand outline hard to see.
substitutions: Use turkey or roasted vegetables instead of ham.
storage: Cover and refrigerate components separately for up to one day before assembly.

title: Sausage Monster Charcuterie Board
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A playful Halloween charcuterie board with a sausage-and-cheese monster face, crisp crackers and fresh produce for contrast.
instructions: Set a wide board on a stable surface and gather all the components first, separating crisp crackers from ingredients that can release moisture.
Arrange sliced sausages in a rounded face shape, leaving a clear space near the top for eyes and along the bottom for a simple cheese toothy smile.
Place two cheese rounds near the top of the sausage circle and centre olive slices on them so the monster has bold, easy-to-recognise eyes.
Line the lower edge with small cheddar triangles or cubes to suggest teeth while keeping the pieces easy for guests to pick up.
Create colourful hair around the top with red pepper strips, then use cucumber rounds and cherry tomatoes to widen the board without hiding the face.
Fill remaining spaces with crackers, keeping at least one cracker group away from moist vegetables so it stays crisp throughout the party.
Add mozzarella pearls and extra olives in little clusters for variety rather than scattering them randomly across the monster outline.
Serve immediately or cover loosely and chill for a short time, bringing the board out before crackers lose their crunch.
tips: Place the face features before filling the board's outer edges.
commonMistakes: Warm sausage slices can soften nearby crackers.
substitutions: Use plant-based cocktail sausages for a meat-free version.
storage: Keep covered in the refrigerator for up to one day; add crackers just before serving.

title: Wrapped Halloween Cheese Ball
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A creamy herb cheese ball wrapped in cucumber ribbons for a fresh, playful Halloween party centrepiece.
instructions: Beat the softened cream cheese, cheddar, chives, lemon juice and garlic powder until the mixture is evenly seasoned and can hold a rounded shape.
Scrape the cheese mixture onto a sheet of baking paper and use clean hands to form a tight ball with no cracks around the sides.
Chill the ball for at least one hour so the surface firms enough to support the cucumber decoration without flattening.
Use a vegetable peeler to make long thin cucumber ribbons, then pat them dry so moisture does not make the cheese ball slippery.
Lay the ribbons across the chilled ball in criss-crossing bands, leaving narrow gaps so the pale cheese still reads as a mummy-style wrap.
Add olive slices near the front as eyes, then move the finished ball carefully to a platter with crackers and crisp vegetable sticks.
Keep the platter chilled until close to serving time, because the cheese softens quickly in a warm party room.
Use a small spreading knife for the cheese ball and replace it with a clean utensil if it touches crackers or other shared food.
tips: Dry the cucumber thoroughly before decorating.
commonMistakes: Warm cream cheese loses the rounded shape.
substitutions: Use dairy-free cream cheese and shredded cheese if needed.
storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to three days.

title: Edible Red Party Sauce
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A bright berry dipping sauce with a glossy finish for fruit, cookies and Halloween dessert boards.
instructions: Combine the berries, sugar, lemon juice and salt in a small saucepan and warm over medium heat until the fruit starts to release its juices.
Press larger berries gently with a spoon so the sauce becomes textured and spoonable while still keeping small pieces for a natural fruit flavour.
Whisk the cornstarch with cold water in a separate cup until completely smooth; adding dry starch directly to hot fruit makes hard lumps.
Stir the slurry into the simmering berries and continue stirring until the sauce turns glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Remove the pan from the heat and cool the sauce for ten minutes, because it will thicken further as the natural fruit pectin sets.
For a smoother dip, push the warm sauce through a fine sieve; for a rustic party bowl, leave the berry pieces in place.
Spoon into a clean serving bowl and surround it with apple slices, strawberries, cookies or cake cubes just before guests arrive.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly and rewarm gently if a softer dipping consistency is wanted the next day.
tips: Use frozen berries directly; thawing is unnecessary.
commonMistakes: Boiling hard after thickening can make the sauce dull and overly sticky.
substitutions: Use cranberry juice with raspberries for a sharper flavour.
storage: Refrigerate in a sealed container for up to five days.

title: Creepy Deviled Egg Eyeballs
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Classic deviled eggs dressed with olive pupils and fine pepper details for an easy Halloween platter.
ingredients: thin strips of roasted red pepper
instructions: Place the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water, bring just to a boil, then cover and remove from the heat for a gentle, even cook.
After twelve minutes, transfer the eggs to ice water so the shells loosen and the yolks stay bright rather than developing a grey ring.
Peel the cooled eggs, halve them lengthwise and carefully lift the yolks into a bowl while keeping the whites intact for the platter.
Mash the yolks with mayonnaise, Dijon, pickle brine, salt and pepper until smooth enough to pipe but not loose enough to run.
Pipe or spoon the filling into each white half, building a small rounded mound that gives the olive eye decoration a stable base.
Set an olive slice on each mound as a pupil, then add a few delicate roasted-pepper strips around it for a playful eye detail.
Arrange the eggs on a chilled plate so they cannot slide, keeping the decorated sides facing upward for the strongest visual effect.
Serve cold and return the platter to refrigeration if it sits out for more than two hours.
tips: Older eggs usually peel more cleanly than very fresh eggs.
commonMistakes: Overcooking makes yolks dry and difficult to mash.
substitutions: Use Greek yogurt for part of the mayonnaise.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to two days.

title: Pizza Skulls
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Cheesy pizza pockets baked in skull molds for a crisp, shareable Halloween snack.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and grease a skull-shaped baking pan thoroughly, including the eye sockets and small details where dough can stick.
Roll the pizza dough into a thin even sheet and cut portions slightly larger than each mold cavity so they can cover the filling completely.
Press one dough portion into every cavity, using fingertips to reach the skull contours without tearing the dough at the narrow edges.
Add a teaspoon of pizza sauce, mozzarella, sausage and bell pepper to each cavity, stopping below the rim so the filling cannot burst out.
Place a second dough piece over each filled cavity, press around the edges to seal, and trim away excess dough for neat individual skulls.
Brush the tops with a little olive oil and sprinkle with Italian seasoning, then cut a tiny steam slit where the design will hide it.
Bake until the dough is browned and firm around the edges, allowing the pan to cool briefly before trying to remove the hot pockets.
Turn the skulls out carefully and serve with warmed pizza sauce, checking the filling temperature before children take a first bite.
tips: Do not overfill the cavities; a small amount gives the cleanest skull shape.
commonMistakes: Opening hot pockets immediately can release very hot cheese.
substitutions: Use sautéed mushrooms instead of sausage.
storage: Refrigerate for up to three days and reheat in the oven.

title: Spooky Baked Brie
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Warm baked brie topped with a pastry spiderweb and olive spider for a simple Halloween starter.
ingredients: crackers and pear slices for serving
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and line a small baking sheet with parchment, giving the brie enough flat space so melted cheese stays contained.
Place the brie in the centre of the pastry and spread fig jam over the top, keeping the filling away from the lower pastry edge.
Fold the pastry around the cheese and turn the parcel seam-side down, then trim a separate pastry strip into thin lengths for the spiderweb decoration.
Lay the strips across the parcel in a loose web pattern, pressing only their ends into the surface so the design rises as the pastry bakes.
Shape a small olive spider from one olive half and thin slivers, placing it near the centre after the pastry has been brushed with egg.
Brush exposed pastry with egg wash, avoiding large pools in the web lines that could blur the decorative pattern during baking.
Bake until the pastry is deeply golden and the cheese feels soft when pressed gently through the crust, usually without needing to cut it open.
Rest five minutes, then serve with crackers and pear slices while the centre is creamy but not dangerously hot.
tips: Use chilled pastry so the web strips keep their definition.
commonMistakes: Cutting immediately lets the cheese run out before the pastry can support it.
substitutions: Use cranberry relish in place of fig jam.
storage: Best served fresh; refrigerate leftovers for up to two days.

title: Ratloaf Meatloaf
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A savory mouse-shaped meatloaf with herb potatoes and roasted vegetables for a playful Halloween supper.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and line a rimmed pan so any rendered fat stays contained.
Mix beef, egg, crumbs, onion, ketchup, Worcestershire, salt and pepper only until combined; heavy mixing makes meatloaf dense.
Shape the mixture into a long teardrop with a rounded nose and a narrower tail end, then place it on the lined pan.
Bake until the centre reaches 71°C on an instant-read thermometer, then rest ten minutes before adding the olive eyes and chive whiskers.
Slice with a sharp knife and serve with roasted vegetables or mashed potatoes while the decorative details stay in place.
tips: Use a thermometer rather than judging doneness from color.
commonMistakes: Packing the mixture tightly produces a tough loaf.
substitutions: Ground turkey works with an extra tablespoon of olive oil.
storage: Refrigerate covered leftovers for up to three days.

title: Chocolate Mice
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Small chocolate truffle mice with almond ears and licorice tails for a gentle Halloween dessert tray.
instructions: Chop the chocolate finely so the warm cream can melt it evenly without scorching.
Pour hot cream over the chocolate with butter, wait one minute, then stir slowly until glossy and smooth.
Chill the ganache until it is firm enough to scoop, then roll tablespoon portions into slightly pointed ovals.
Roll each oval lightly in cocoa, press in two almond ears and add a short licorice tail at the rounded end.
Add candy eyes just before serving and keep the mice chilled until the tray is needed.
tips: Cold hands keep the ganache from softening while shaping.
commonMistakes: Warm ganache will not hold a mouse shape.
substitutions: Use sunflower-seed slices instead of almonds for a nut-free decoration.
storage: Refrigerate in one layer for up to five days.

title: Black Bat Chicken Wings
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Crisp oven wings glazed with a dark balsamic barbecue sauce and served with a bat-themed garnish.
instructions: Pat the wings very dry, then toss with baking powder, paprika, salt and pepper for a crisper oven finish.
Arrange on a rack over a tray and roast at 220°C, turning once, until the skin is crisp and the thickest pieces reach 74°C.
Simmer barbecue sauce, balsamic and molasses briefly until the glaze is shiny and deep brown.
Toss the hot wings in just enough glaze to coat without making the skin soggy.
Serve immediately with a separate bowl of sauce and vegetable sticks.
tips: Dry wings are the key to crisp skin.
commonMistakes: Glazing before roasting can burn the sugars.
substitutions: Use tamari and honey for a different dark glaze.
storage: Refrigerate for up to three days; reheat in the oven.

title: Mini Monster Meatloaf Bites
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Individual glazed meatloaf bites with vegetable faces, sized for a Halloween buffet or family dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and grease twelve muffin cups.
Stir beef, egg, oats, milk, garlic powder and half the ketchup until evenly combined.
Divide into the cups and smooth the tops, leaving room for the glaze to set around the edges.
Brush with remaining ketchup and bake until each centre reaches 71°C.
Rest five minutes, then add olive and pepper faces before serving.
tips: A small scoop keeps every bite the same size.
commonMistakes: Decorating before baking lets vegetables burn.
substitutions: Use ground chicken with a little olive oil.
storage: Refrigerate for three days or freeze for one month.

title: Monster Cheese Ball
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A bright herb-and-cheddar cheese ball decorated with vegetable eyes for a cheerful Halloween snack table.
instructions: Beat cream cheese, cheddar, parsley and onion powder until no streaks remain.
Shape into a round ball on baking paper and chill until firm.
Roll the chilled ball through pistachios, pressing them lightly into the surface.
Use olive slices and carrot strips to create a simple monster face.
Serve cold with crackers, celery and apple slices.
tips: Chill before coating so the nuts stay on the outside.
commonMistakes: Soft cheese ball spreads across the platter.
substitutions: Use toasted seeds instead of pistachios.
storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to three days.

title: Jack-O-Lantern Stuffed Peppers
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Orange bell peppers carved with friendly faces and filled with seasoned rice, beans and cheese.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and cut lids from the peppers, removing seeds and membranes.
Use a small knife to cut simple triangle eyes and a smile into one side of each pepper.
Mix rice, beans, corn, salsa, cumin and half the cheese in a bowl.
Fill the peppers loosely, top with remaining cheese and replace the lids at a slight angle.
Bake until peppers are tender and filling is hot throughout, then serve upright.
tips: Do not cut face openings too large or filling can spill.
commonMistakes: Overpacking prevents the rice centre from heating evenly.
substitutions: Add cooked ground turkey for a meatier filling.
storage: Refrigerate for up to three days.

title: Witch Hat Dippers
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Crisp tortilla cones with seasoned cream-cheese filling, shaped as savory witch hats for dipping.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and brush both sides of tortilla wedges lightly with oil.
Bake wedges until crisp, then cool completely so they stay pointed and crunchy.
Mix cream cheese, cheddar, scallions and taco seasoning until spreadable.
Spoon the filling onto round cracker bases and stand a tortilla cone in the centre of each one.
Serve with salsa alongside so guests can dip without softening the hats in advance.
tips: Assemble close to serving so the tortilla stays crisp.
commonMistakes: Warm cones soften the cheese filling.
substitutions: Use bean dip instead of cream cheese.
storage: Store components separately for up to two days.

title: Jack-O-Lantern Beef Hand Pies
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Flaky individual beef pies with carved pumpkin-style pastry tops for a portable Halloween meal.
instructions: Cook onion and beef until browned, then stir in tomato paste, thyme and stock and reduce until thick.
Cool the filling so it will not melt the pastry before baking.
Cut pastry rounds, spoon filling onto half, and cut simple jack-o-lantern faces into the matching top rounds.
Seal edges with egg wash and crimp firmly, leaving the facial cutouts open as steam vents.
Bake at 200°C until golden and rest five minutes before serving.
tips: Thick filling keeps the hand pies sealed.
commonMistakes: Hot filling turns pastry greasy and hard to seal.
substitutions: Use lentils and mushrooms in place of beef.
storage: Refrigerate for three days and reheat in an oven.

title: Spooky Calzone Snake
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A long mozzarella-and-pepperoni calzone coiled into a friendly snake for a Halloween pizza night.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a wide tray with baking paper.
Roll the dough into a long rectangle and spread sauce down the middle, leaving a clear edge.
Add mozzarella and pepperoni, fold over the dough and pinch the seam closed.
Curve the filled rope into a loose snake shape, tapering one end for the head.
Brush with egg, add olive eyes and a pepper tongue, then bake until golden and hot in the centre.
tips: Keep the filling narrow so the seam closes.
commonMistakes: Too much sauce causes the snake to split.
substitutions: Use cooked mushrooms instead of pepperoni.
storage: Refrigerate for up to three days.

title: Octodogs
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Hot dog octopuses with crisp curled legs, served with a simple mustard and ketchup dip.
instructions: Cut each hot dog in half, leaving the rounded end intact for the head.
Make four lengthwise cuts through the lower half to create eight slim legs.
Pan-sear in a little oil, turning gently as the legs curl and the cut edges brown.
Set the octodogs upright on a platter and add mustard dots or food-safe candy eyes.
Serve hot with ketchup and mustard for dipping.
tips: Cut legs evenly so they curl at a similar rate.
commonMistakes: Deep cuts through the head split the octopus apart.
substitutions: Use plant-based hot dogs.
storage: Best served fresh; refrigerate leftovers for two days.

title: Hot Dog Mummies
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Tender hot dogs wrapped in golden pastry strips with tiny mustard eyes for a quick Halloween tray.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and line a baking tray.
Cut dough into thin uneven strips to create a loose wrapped appearance.
Wind strips around each hot dog, leaving a small open space near one end for the face.
Brush the dough lightly with beaten egg and bake until the strips are puffed and golden.
Add two mustard dots after baking and serve warm with ketchup.
tips: Leave small gaps so the dough looks like bandages.
commonMistakes: Wrapping too tightly stops the pastry from puffing.
substitutions: Use vegetarian hot dogs.
storage: Refrigerate for up to two days and reheat in an oven.

title: Mummy Pizza
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A crisp personal pizza covered with mozzarella bandages and olive eyes for an easy Halloween meal.
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C and place the pitas on a baking sheet.
Spread a thin layer of sauce, leaving a narrow crust edge.
Lay mozzarella in loose uneven strips so the red sauce shows between the bandages.
Add olive slices in a small uncovered face space, then season lightly.
Bake until the pita is crisp and the cheese bubbles, then cool briefly before slicing.
tips: Use low-moisture mozzarella for clear strips.
commonMistakes: Heavy sauce makes the pita soft.
substitutions: Use naan or a prepared pizza base.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers for two days.

title: Spider Hot Dogs
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Mini hot dog spiders with pretzel-stick legs, made for a quick kid-friendly Halloween platter.
instructions: Cut each hot dog into two short pieces and make four shallow holes along each side.
Press pretzel halves into the holes as legs, keeping the centre piece stable.
Warm in a skillet with a small amount of oil until the hot dogs are heated through.
Add tiny mustard eyes after cooking so they stay visible.
Serve at once with ketchup, replacing pretzels if any soften on the platter.
tips: Use sturdy pretzel sticks so the legs do not snap.
commonMistakes: Boiling makes the pretzels soft.
substitutions: Use mini sausages for smaller spiders.
storage: Best served immediately.

title: Mini Meatloaf Ghosts
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Tender individual meatloaves topped with piped potato ghosts for a warm Halloween dinner.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and divide the seasoned meatloaf mixture into greased muffin cups.
Bake until each centre reaches 71°C, then let the portions rest while preparing smooth warm mashed potatoes.
Pipe the potatoes in tall swirls over each meatloaf to create a ghost shape.
Press two tiny olive pieces into every potato ghost as eyes.
Return to the oven for a few minutes only to warm the topping, then serve.
tips: Warm potatoes pipe more smoothly than cold potatoes.
commonMistakes: Overfilled cups spill fat around the potato topping.
substitutions: Use sweet-potato mash for a slightly sweeter ghost.
storage: Refrigerate for three days.

title: Baked Mummy Jalapeño Poppers
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Cream-cheese jalapeño poppers wrapped in light pastry strips and baked until crisp.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C, halve the jalapeños and scrape out seeds and membranes with gloves if sensitive to chile oil.
Mix cream cheese and cheddar, then fill each pepper half without mounding above the edge.
Cut dough into thin strips and wind them over the filling, leaving a small face gap.
Bake until peppers soften and pastry is golden.
Add olive eyes after baking and cool five minutes before serving because the filling stays very hot.
tips: Wear gloves when handling cut jalapeños.
commonMistakes: Overfilling causes the cheese to bubble out.
substitutions: Use mini sweet peppers for a mild version.
storage: Refrigerate for up to three days.

title: Shrimp Cocktail Brain Dip
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A chilled shrimp cocktail dip piped into a playful brain-like swirl for a Halloween seafood starter.
instructions: Blend cream cheese, half the cocktail sauce and horseradish until smooth enough to pipe.
Fold in chopped shrimp and lemon zest, keeping some shrimp pieces visible for texture.
Spoon the mixture into a piping bag with a round tip and pipe two winding brain-like lobes onto a chilled plate.
Drizzle remaining cocktail sauce lightly through the grooves for contrast.
Serve cold with crackers and keep refrigerated between servings.
tips: Chill the plate first so the piped shape holds.
commonMistakes: Warm cream cheese mixture spreads instead of forming ridges.
substitutions: Use finely chopped imitation crab if preferred.
storage: Refrigerate for up to one day.

title: Mummified Meatballs in Potato Skin Coffins
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Crisp potato-skin coffins holding saucy meatballs with cheese-strip mummy wraps.
instructions: Halve baked potatoes and scoop out most of the flesh, leaving a sturdy potato-skin shell.
Trim the shells into simple coffin shapes and roast cut-side up until crisp.
Warm meatballs in marinara until hot throughout, then place one or two in each potato coffin.
Lay mozzarella strips across the meatballs as loose mummy wraps.
Broil briefly until cheese melts and finish with olive eyes before serving.
tips: Crisp the potato skins before adding sauce.
commonMistakes: Excess sauce makes the skins collapse.
substitutions: Use plant-based meatballs.
storage: Refrigerate components separately for two days.

title: Crescent Mummy Hot Dogs
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Bite-size crescent-wrapped hot dogs with a crisp flaky finish for Halloween party snacking.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and line a tray with parchment.
Cut crescent dough into narrow strips and wind each around a cocktail sausage.
Leave a small open face area and brush pastry with egg for even browning.
Bake until the dough is puffed and golden and sausages are hot.
Add mustard eyes after baking and serve warm.
tips: Use a small brush for neat egg wash.
commonMistakes: Thick dough strips stay pale in the centre.
substitutions: Use vegetarian cocktail sausages.
storage: Refrigerate for two days.

title: Pumpkin Sloppy Joes
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Savory ground-beef sandwiches enriched with pumpkin purée, tomato and warm spices for autumn.
instructions: Brown the beef and onion in a skillet, breaking the meat into small pieces and draining excess fat if needed.
Stir in pumpkin purée, tomato sauce, brown sugar and paprika until the sauce is smooth.
Simmer gently until thick enough to spoon onto buns without running off.
Toast the buns lightly to give them a barrier against the sauce.
Fill buns just before serving and offer pickles or slaw alongside.
tips: Use plain pumpkin purée, not sweetened pie filling.
commonMistakes: Boiling hard can make the pumpkin sauce catch.
substitutions: Use lentils for a vegetarian filling.
storage: Refrigerate filling for up to three days.

title: Spider Deviled Eggs
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Creamy deviled eggs topped with olive spiders for a classic, protein-rich Halloween appetizer.
instructions: Hard-cook the eggs, cool in ice water and peel them carefully.
Halve each egg and mash yolks with mayonnaise, Dijon, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Spoon or pipe the filling into the egg whites.
Cut each olive into a body and thin legs, arranging one spider over each filled egg.
Keep chilled until serving and refrigerate promptly after the buffet.
tips: Use a sharp paring knife to cut neat olive legs.
commonMistakes: Warm eggs make the filling loose.
substitutions: Use Greek yogurt for part of the mayonnaise.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to two days.
